Fatty-acid oxidation defect with myopathy; neuropathy 11/14 and dilated cardiomyopathy 8/11. Cholestasis 2/15 and retinopathy 2/16 are below threshold.
LMF1-related lipid metabolism disorder; subcutaneous fat loss reported in 1/1 patient. Pancreatitis and diabetes are separately diagnosed associated diseases.

Defining severe T-cell deficiency with lymphopenia, congenital alopecia and nail dystrophy; core features occur in 80-99%.
Reactive eosinophilia with tissue injury; skin involvement ~50% and pulmonary involvement ~40% in HES. Secondary-subtype frequencies vary; cardiac damage is less consistent.
Skeletal dysplasia with fractures and cortical defects plus defining dentinogenesis imperfecta; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Central impairment of auditory recognition despite usually normal hearing; no intrinsic ear disorder is established.
Parasitic myiasis with larvae invading and destroying living tissue, usually in cutaneous wounds; other anatomical sites are variable.
Motor neuropathy with defining vocal-cord paresis and impaired laryngeal function; the larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Defining neutropenia, monocytopenia and marrow hypoplasia cause immune deficiency; congenital sensorineural deafness is a core feature.
Defining brain malformations, renal and ureteral agenesis/hypoplasia, and generalized arthrogryposis; reproductive malformations have no axis.
Iron overload directly causes hepatic necrosis and fibrosis. Cardiac and endocrine abnormalities are occasional; viral hepatitis is a separate disease.
Atrophy and inflammation of tongue papillae; the tongue and oral mucosa belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Congenital duplication and fusion of digits, including abnormal thumb phalanges; no other organ involvement is established.
Sarcoma originating in the kidney; spindle-cell histology does not establish skeletal muscle involvement.
Loss of thyroid endocrine function following surgery defines this condition.
Fungal infection predominantly producing cutaneous and subcutaneous nodules; pulmonary and disseminated disease are minority presentations.
Inherited platelet aggregation defect; epistaxis, bruising and mucosal bleeding do not establish separate organ damage.
Cowden disease is defined by cutaneous and oral mucosal hamartomas; thyroid nodules reported in 1/2. Associated cancers are separate predisposition outcomes.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay occur in 8/8; structural spinal involvement with kyphoscoliosis occurs in 4/8.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, profound developmental impairment and cerebral white-matter/callosal abnormalities.
Developmental deformity of the sternum and thoracic skeleton; clinically important cardiac or pulmonary impairment is not established in most patients.
Inherited susceptibility to febrile seizures defines a neurologic disorder; fever does not establish an infectious disease mechanism.
